questions.question: What can you do to reduce your chances of being in a crash?

options.text: Do not use your turn signals when changing lanes.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Watch about five feet ahead of your motorcycle while riding.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to communicate. Keep space around your motorcycle. Look ahead, behind, and to the sides. Always be ready to avoid sudden hazards.

questions.question: Proper riding clothes provide all of the following, except:

options.text: Comfort.
Protection in a collision.
Protection from the cold.
Discomfort.

questions.correctAnswerText: Discomfort.
questions.explanation: Proper riding clothes protect you from injury in a crash. They also protect you from heat, cold, and other weather. They do not cause discomfort.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can your body eliminate per hour?

options.text: One
Two
Three
Four

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour on average. The time it takes to lower blood alcohol content varies. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, where should you stay?

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Look to your left frequently.
Use your rearview mirrors more frequently than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, stay on the side of your lane away from them. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out. This gives you distance from hazards.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not necessary if you have a windshield.
It only protects your eyes.
It protects more than just your eyes.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects more than just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Rely on your mirrors to show you all of your surroundings.
Point in the direction of the lane change.
Speed up to get ahead of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: What percentage of braking power does the front brake provide?

options.text: 10 percent
25 percent
50 percent
75 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 75 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 75 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Which of these should a passenger never do?

options.text: Wear a helmet.
Lean when the operator leans.
Wear clothing that is tight.
Ride sidesaddle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride sidesaddle.
questions.explanation: Passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. It is recommended for all riders. Passengers should wear snug clothing and lean with the operator. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: Why should motorcyclists in a group avoid riding in pairs?

options.text: A merging driver may not see both riders.
Reflections from both helmets may make it difficult for the riders to see.
Riding in pairs does not allow riders the necessary space to maneuver.
It is too difficult for riders on the left side of a pairing to exit a highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in pairs does not allow riders the necessary space to maneuver.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, motorcyclists should not ride in pairs. Neither rider will have enough room to maneuver and avoid hazards.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chance of having a crash?

options.text: Make sure other drivers can see you.
Hide your plans from other drivers.
Always stay within one foot of another vehicle.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, always be visible to other drivers. Signal your turns, use your brake light, and position your motorcycle correctly. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: What should you do to stay in control of your motorcycle while turning?

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright without leaning.
Look ahead through the turn to see what comes next.
Stop completely before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn to see what comes next.
questions.explanation: To stay in control through a turn, look ahead through it by turning only your head. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder.
Signal and check your mirrors.
Look over your shoulder and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see if any vehicles are in your way before you move.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are tired while riding.
When you will slow down where other drivers don't expect it.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down where other drivers don't expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are hard to see compared to larger vehicles. Flash your brake light before slowing down in unexpected places, like the middle of a block or near an alley, so other drivers notice you stopping.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both actions at the same time.
Always brake first, then swerve.
Use only the brakes instead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, do these actions one at a time. You can either brake then swerve, or swerve then brake. Never do both at the same time.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist stop other vehicles from sharing their lane?

options.text: Ride in the left side of the lane.
Ride in the center of the lane.
Give dirty looks if another driver enters your lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill up the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When another driver might try to squeeze into your lane next to you, ride in the center of the lane to discourage them.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider be ready for when passing parked cars?

options.text: Empty parking spaces.
A car suddenly pulling out of a parking space into traffic.
Parking meters.
Other drivers seeing you and staying out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car suddenly pulling out of a parking space into traffic.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, be ready for one to suddenly pull into traffic. Ride on the left side of your lane when passing parked cars on your right to stay as far away as possible from this danger.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with other drivers mean?

options.text: It means they see you.
It guarantees they will let you go.
It doesn't always mean they see you.
It is not worth trying.

questions.correctAnswerText: It doesn't always mean they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume eye contact means a driver will let you go. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but still do not notice them.

questions.question: What should you do on a long motorcycle trip?

options.text: Take as few breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel tired.
Wear warm clothes to protect from cold wind.
Ride more than 12 hours per day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear warm clothes to protect from cold wind.
questions.explanation: To stay safe on a long trip, dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day and take breaks at least every two hours. Avoid caffeine and other stimulants because they cause extreme tiredness when they wear off.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power does the front brake provide?

options.text: About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent
About 95 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. The front brake provides at least 70 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power.
